title: When the Wreck Falls
premise: Blacklisted mountain guide Oscar Oyelaran is salvaging a living on a monsoon-battered coast when the tide uncovers a sea cave said to hold the lost ledgers of a colonial shipping syndicate — proof that could clear his name and ruin the dynasty that blacklisted him. Hunted by the syndicate's fixer, he shelters with Mara Voss, a disgraced maritime archivist whose duty to return the documents legally collides with his hunger for justice outside the law. As the monsoon traps them with a leaking boat and dwindling supplies, they fall in love while racing to cross the glacier pass before calving season seals it for another year. In the end Oscar chooses to hand the ledgers to an international tribunal through Mara's channels rather than sell them, clearing his name at the cost of the revenge he wanted — and winning a future he never expected.
about_author: Sable Ishikawa is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent six seasons guiding in coastal ranges before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people the mountains and seas refuse to forgive.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps No Receipts
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Broke and blacklisted, Oscar takes a dubious salvage job hauling storm debris after a record tide, and finds a cave mouth exposed where charts show solid rock. Inside: a rusted strongbox stamped with the Meridian Syndicate crest. The beat is wary hope — a man who has stopped believing in luck touching it anyway.

chapters.title: Paper Older Than My Sins
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The strongbox holds ledgers proving the Syndicate sank its own ships to collect insurance and framed guides like Oscar as scapegoats. He photographs pages, but the cave's collapse behind him signals someone knew he'd come. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Introduce Mara Voss, an archivist under tribunal subpoena to recover the same ledgers, and Aldous Renk, the Syndicate fixer who offers Oscar money for silence and a boat ticket out of the country. Oscar refuses; Renk burns his lodging. Beat: the trap closing gently, politely.

chapters.title: A Stranger With a Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Monsoon hits early. Oscar and Mara, forced together by circumstance, flee downcoast in her hull-cracked research ketch, bailing water and trading suspicions — she thinks he'll sell the ledgers; he thinks she'll bury them in procedure. Beat: grudging alliance born of necessity.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A quiet chapter at anchor in a fishing cove: Mara reveals her father was a Syndicate captain who drowned in one of the staged wrecks; her duty-bound career is penance. Oscar admits the debt he carries is to a dead climbing partner the blacklist dishonored. Beat: intimacy through confession.

chapters.title: Renk's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Renk's men board them at a fuel stop; the ledgers are nearly seized before Oscar rigs a decoy drop and they escape into open water through a squall, the boat taking worse damage. First real violence of the book. Beat: adrenaline and the cost of running.

chapters.title: The Glacier Opens Once
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the fjord below the glacier pass with days left before calving season closes the route. Renk has bought the local pilots; their only way through is the route that got Oscar's partner killed. Beat: dread — walking back into the shape of his worst day.

chapters.title: Love Against the Icefall
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The ascent. Oscar leads them up the unstable route while ice groans overhead; when a serac release strands Mara, he anchors himself and pulls her out, choosing her over the ledgers strapped to his back. Beat: love made physical, decisive, undeniable.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. On the far side, Renk waits with the border patrol bought and paid for — until Mara reveals she transmitted ledger copies to the tribunal from the cove's radio relay days earlier. Renk's leverage dies mid-sentence as warrants land. Climax: the corrupt machine undone by patience, not force.

chapters.title: When the Wreck Falls Quiet
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later: the tribunal clears Oscar's name, the Syndicate collapses, and the original cave is sealed as a heritage site. Oscar and Mara guide together under their own flag, the compass finally pointing somewhere instead of away. Beat: earned peace — justice served, love chosen, debts paid.
